fact: Oracle launched its public cloud region in Casablanca, Morocco, announced up and running on 7 April 2026 (one availability domain reportedly available since late February 2026); Oracle calls it the first hyperscaler region in North Africa.
N+One Datacenters hosts Oracle's Casablanca cloud region and operates six data centre buildings (4.5 MW IT, 4,000 sqm) split between Nouaceur and Settat, per its website; date is the region's launch.

DatacenterDynamics reports Maroc Datacenter (MDC, founded 2017) operates a single 2,000 sqm data centre in the Rabat area, merged into 3MDC with Munisys and Medasys; as_of is the article date, which gives no opening date.

Tech Africa News reports Orange Maroc inaugurated its Orange Tech data centre (1.5 MW initial capacity, near Nouaceur) for hosting, cloud and cybersecurity services; as_of is the article date, which gives no inauguration date.

Forci News reports DXC Technology Morocco, a DXC and CDG joint venture, obtained Uptime Institute Tier III Tier Certification of Constructed Facility (TCCF) for its DXC-CDG data centre, which it says serves current and future customers.
DatacenterDynamics reports Maroc Datacenter operates a single 2,000 sqm data centre in the Rabat area and hosts an OVHcloud Local Zone there for customers; as_of is the article date.

N+One, described as a data centre operator that will host Oracle's OCI infrastructure for the Moroccan region, operates data centres in Nouaceur and Settat, being expanded by 2MW to 8MW total by end-2024 (DCD, 14 March 2024; as_of is the article date, none given).

N+One Datacenters, a Casablanca-based data centre operator founded in 2008, operates two data centres in Morocco (unnamed here); a third, 2,000 sqm, at Nouaceur is only planned for later in 2024 (DCD, 3 January 2024; as_of is the article date, none given).

N+One Datacenters, a Casablanca-based operator, operates two data centers in Morocco, described as market-leading facilities serving customers (DatacenterDynamics, on AIIM's investment); the article gives no facility names; date taken from the article's publication.

inwi's datacentres at Sapino (Casablanca) and Technopolis (Rabat/Salé) are operational, as are Tanger, Oujda, Meknès and Agadir, offering about 4,000 m2 of dedicated or shared hosting space to business customers; Settat and Marrakech were planned for 2023; dated 2023-06-14 per the article's publication.

UM6P formally opened its Benguerir Data Center, built with OCP Group, which also houses managed cloud services provider Atlas Cloud Services (the document gives 'published' date as the opening date; it does not say the centre rents capacity to others beyond hosting Atlas).
The Benguerir Data Center, now open, is described as Tier IV Design certified (design certification, 5MW IT load; certifier not named in the text).
inwi opened its fourth data center, 1,000 sq m at Rabat Technopolis, to offer hosting services to Moroccan companies; inwi says it now has 4,000 sq m under management.

inwi says the new Rabat Technopolis data center holds Uptime Institute Tier Certification of Design Documents (TCDD), with Constructed Facility certification due soon (tier level not stated in the text).
Maroc Telecom's enterprise data center in Casablanca, launched May 2017, sells colocation (full or half racks) to businesses; about ten companies had signed up by the 26 June 2018 press visit.
Maroc Telecom's Casablanca city-centre data center (two rooms of 225 and 155 sq m, up to 100 racks) offers server hosting to SMEs from MAD 11,000 a month; date is the article's, 2018-06-27.
N+One Datacenters launched its second data center, 4MW, 80km from Casablanca, as disaster recovery for its 5,000 sq m Casablanca site; date is the article's, 2017-10-04.
The new N+One data center is stated to be PCI DSS and Tier III Design certified (certifier not named).

Medafrica Systems (Medasys) inaugurated the Maroc Datacenter at Temara on 19 September 2017, described by the Ministry as a cloud computing platform offering managed services to SMEs, large companies and public administrations; the page says it was designed according to the Tier III standard, with no certification stated.

Orange Maroc inaugurated its Orange Tech data centre at Nouaceur (1.5 MW initial capacity, 15,000 square metres, Uptime Institute certification of unstated tier) on 19 November 2025, as part of a B2B offer of cloud services and dedicated IT infrastructure sold to enterprises (Morocco World News).
Oracle launched a cloud region in Morocco in March 2024 in collaboration with data centre operator N+One (DatacenterDynamics, passing mention).

OCP Group, with UM6P, launched the Benguerir Data Center (2,000 m2 of white rooms, 5 MW IT load, Benguerir Tech Park), offering data centre and cloud services to national operators; as_of is the article date, which gives no other date.
Infomediaire states the Benguerir Data Center, launched by OCP Group, is certified Tier III and Tier IV by the Uptime Institute; as_of is the article date.

Orange Maroc says AWS Wavelength compute and storage is deployed in its Casablanca data centre, so customers can store and process data in Morocco and pay in dirhams (interview; zone live by February 2025).

Orange Maroc states its Casablanca data centre hosting the AWS Wavelength zone meets Tier III Design and Facilities standards (operator statement; no certifier named); date is the article's publication date.

Orange operates two data centres in Casablanca, one a 1MW facility (DC2, built 2015) bought from Etix Everywhere in 2021, and AWS has launched a Wavelength Zone in Orange's Casablanca data centres for customers' applications.

N+ONE DATACENTERS, described as an African data centre owner and operator, is stated to have built market-leading facilities and existing campuses in Morocco serving customers, per the AIIM release on its USD 90 million joint venture; the facilities are not individually named and the document gives no opening date, so the date is the publication date.

DatacenterDynamics reported in August 2023 that Moroccan operator N+One Datacenters has existing campuses in Morocco and an existing portfolio of digital infrastructure assets it contributes to a new data centre and cloud services platform backed by AIIM; no tier rating is stated.
Aujourd'hui le Maroc states that Oracle has opened its first cloud region in Casablanca and is preparing a second at Settat.
Atlas Cloud Services offers its Benguerir data center to institutions and businesses, with 2,000 m2 of white space and 5MW IT load.
